stories.title: Designers are told to keep up with AI
stories.summary: Designers are being urged to improve their skills as AI becomes more proficient at design work. The industry is currently focused on reviewing portfolios, hiring processes, and the mechanics of how designers explain their creative decisions. Apparently, being a human is no longer the only requirement for the job.

stories.title: A manifesto for the post-AI bubble
stories.summary: Computers were intended to be tools for people, but the AI bubble has fostered a culture of fatalism that uses technology to push people around. The authors suggest this will eventually change, though they offer no specific timeline for when the shift might occur.

stories.title: Usability remains a five-part challenge
stories.summary: Usability is defined by how easily people complete tasks using an interface. Jakob Nielsen’s updated guide identifies five components: learnability, efficiency, memorability, error handling, and satisfaction. The original 2012 guide remains available for those interested in the history of how people struggle with software.

stories.title: The agent harness manages AI execution
stories.summary: An agent harness is the software surrounding an AI model that runs its execution loop, manages tool use, and controls information flow. While two assistants might use the same underlying model, their capabilities differ based on this surrounding support. The model itself is just the engine.

stories.title: Paul Boag to launch UX Insiders community
stories.summary: Paul Boag will launch UX Insiders on January 5, 2027, a paid community for in-house user experience practitioners. The project, partnered with Smashing Magazine, offers weekly calls and a private Slack group. It aims to support solo practitioners who often find themselves without colleagues to consult.

stories.title: Gabby Clark on scaling design systems
stories.summary: Design director Gabby Clark has spent 12 years building design systems for companies like Microsoft and Salesforce. She advocates for combining visual design with systems thinking to create scalable experiences. Her work aims to ensure that digital visions remain cohesive when used by millions of people worldwide.

stories.title: Design errors often bypass final validation
stories.summary: Thirteen design failures, including a lettering error on an iQIYI poster and a buttermilk package redesign, highlight the risks of failing to validate artwork in a real context. Designers often work on flat keylines without mockups. The medium, it seems, is rarely considered until it is printed.

stories.title: Legal discovery faces usability hurdles
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors often send defense counsel terabytes of discovery data on hard drives. While the government considers this a straightforward production of material, the sheer volume creates significant usability problems for the defense. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Workflow integration dictates immersive healthcare success
stories.summary: A study of the REDOCVR program in Catalonia found that the scalability of immersive healthcare tools depends on workflow integration, device logistics, and institutional backing. Clinical content and patient receptivity were secondary factors. The software architecture was fundamentally reshaped by the realities of everyday clinical practice.

stories.title: AI tools reduce workload but weaken design satisfaction
stories.summary: Integrating generative AI into textile design reduces operational workload and speeds up tasks, according to a study of 34 fashion students. However, the use of automated tools simultaneously weakened creative autonomy and personal style. Efficiency, it appears, comes at the cost of the student's own design satisfaction.

stories.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production
stories.summary: Elon Musk announced that Tesla will wind down production of the Cybertruck at its Texas factory around the middle of next year. The vehicle, which launched with promises of unbreakable windows and Mars travel, will see its manufacturing footprint reduced. The deposit holders have been notified.

stories.title: Cybertruck production faces mid-2027 scale back
stories.summary: Tesla is scaling back Cybertruck production at its Texas facility around mid-2027 to prioritize Cybercab robotaxis. While the company has not explicitly stated the vehicle is discontinued, the Texas plant is the only facility equipped to build its specialized parts. The writing is on the wall.

stories.title: The New York Times celebrates 175 years with custom type
stories.summary: For its 175th anniversary, The New York Times paired a custom blackletter mark with archival collage branding. Creative director Jessi Brattengeier led the project, which involved motion designer Kiffer Keegan to ensure static print forms and screen movements evolved together. Custom marks are not routine there.

stories.title: Studio Yukiko uses stone for postmodernist book design
stories.summary: Studio Yukiko designed the Everything At Once catalogue using stone-inspired imagery to represent postmodernism. The cover features a grey stone slab on a red field, with various stone shapes appearing throughout the chapters. The book contains no photographs or collages, just the stone.

stories.title: &Walsh creates identity for film matte software
stories.summary: &Walsh designed the BATCH brand identity using blocked letterforms and film grain to reflect the company's software, which separates people from scenes. The agency adopted a direct voice, claiming that film mattes now take hours instead of months. The brand looks like the tool itself.

stories.title: Dutchscot crafts identity for Brooklyn bar
stories.summary: London studio Dutchscot designed the visual identity for Bar Rêve in Brooklyn, drawing inspiration from Belle Époque Paris. The branding features a wobbly script wordmark and a 222 monogram. The studio avoided Art Nouveau clichés in favor of a mood of optimism and style.

stories.title: ESH Gruppa balances gallery and design studio needs
stories.summary: ESH Gruppa designed the NM Art & Design platform to serve both art collectors and interior designers. The UI pairs gallery pacing with dedicated professional accounts for project management. The platform must accommodate two different types of visitors who are browsing at very different speeds.

stories.title: Toki desk timer focuses on Pomodoro habits
stories.summary: Stanley Pulvirenti and Tommaso Sposito designed the Toki desk timer to turn the Pomodoro Technique into a tactile experience. The device features animated eye states and a coral-red wordmark, intentionally moving away from the aesthetic of cold office gear. Numbers are not the priority.

stories.title: Wolff Olins updates BMG brand identity
stories.summary: Wolff Olins has unveiled a new brand identity for BMG, featuring a faceted triangle symbol designed to function as a play button and connected ecosystem. The studio retained the existing logo for stability, adding a new palette of acid lime, deep blue, and metallic neutrals to the mix.

stories.title: Apple Music Classical adopts monochrome icon
stories.summary: Apple has updated the Apple Music Classical app icon to a black and white design, aligning it with the broader Apple Music rebrand. While the standard music app icon is now flat, the Classical version retains a three-dimensional treatment with subtle lighting and shading. The G-clef remains.

stories.summary: Adobe is integrating NVIDIA RTX Spark superchips into its creative suite, including Photoshop and Premiere. The company claims the hardware optimization delivers up to 2x faster AI processing and editing for users. Adobe is also using NVIDIA Nemotron models to power its Brand Concierge enterprise tool.

stories.title: Figma reports rising AI costs
stories.summary: Figma reported a 43 percent year over year revenue increase to $391.4 million, though its stock fell nearly 4 percent after hours. The company's non-GAAP gross margin slid from 85 percent to 82 percent. CFO Praveer Melwani noted that AI is currently acting as a tax on profits.

stories.title: Meta adds Spaces to Muse agent interface
stories.summary: Meta has introduced Spaces, a feature for its Muse AI agents that allows users to organize conversations into specific topics. Meta describes these as custom experiences that live in the sidebar, where the agent works toward a particular goal. The company calls the agents cuddly helpers.

stories.title: Underdog releases 32MB voice model
stories.summary: Startup Underdog has released a demo game called Woof featuring a 32MB voice model designed to run on edge devices. The game includes a retro-themed room and a typewriter, with an intro that warns users about intrusive cloud providers. The model avoids the need for massive processing power.

stories.title: Physicl raises $10 million for robot simulation
stories.summary: Physicl has raised $10 million in seed funding led by Inovia Capital to develop realistic simulations for robot training. Founder Alex de Vigan is repurposing technology from his previous venture, nfinite, which focused on 3D product renderings for e-commerce. The goal is to solve thorny training problems.

stories.title: Open and closed AI models narrow cyber capability gap
stories.summary: The Vals CyberOffense benchmark found that open-weight model Deepseek V4.1 Flash 1017 achieved a 72.8 percent success rate in breaking into simulated corporate networks. OpenAI's restricted GPT-6 Sol model reached 80.8 percent. The open model costs roughly $3 per run, compared to approximately $22 for the closed version.

stories.title: Canva AI or Adobe Firefly? Choose by finished-asset workflow
stories.summary: Choosing between Canva AI and Adobe Firefly depends on your delivery needs, not the first image produced. Canva suits branded assets and social posts, while Adobe Firefly targets users needing deep refinement and editing control. The deciding factor is whether you need a layout or a raw asset.

stories.title: Adobe offers startups 12 months of free access to creative tools
stories.summary: Adobe is offering startups founded within the last five years and with under $15 million in funding one year of free access to Firefly Pro Plus, Acrobat Studio, and Semrush. The program aims to provide solutions for founders that do not break their startup budget.

stories.title: Adobe provides startups with free access to AI suite
stories.summary: Adobe is offering startups founded in the last five years 12 months of free access to its AI-heavy tools, including Firefly Pro Plus and Acrobat Studio. The initiative aims to provide new businesses with easy solutions that do not break their startup budget.

stories.title: Epic Games makes Quixel Megascans library free indefinitely
stories.summary: Epic Games has made its Quixel Megascans library of 3D and 2D assets free indefinitely. The collection, which includes thousands of photogrammetry-based models and materials, was previously free for a limited time to mark the launch of the Fab marketplace. It is now a permanent resource.

stories.title: Managing Webflow order line items in Zapier
stories.summary: Webflow orders arrive in Zapier as parallel lists, which can cause data mismatches if product names contain commas. Zapier webhooks struggle with this format. Users can employ Looping by Zapier to process items individually or use custom code to avoid silent failures during inventory updates.

stories.title: Building hybrid apps with Webflow Designer and Data APIs
stories.summary: Developers can mount Next.js apps on Webflow sites using Webflow Cloud to enable features like live search and pricing calculators. The process requires a published Webflow collection and a local Node.js toolchain to render results using DevLink export components alongside standard CMS templates.

stories.title: Automating YouTube uploads to Webflow CMS
stories.summary: Teams can use Zapier to automatically convert public YouTube uploads into indexable Webflow CMS pages. The automation uses the New Video in Channel trigger to create live items, removing the manual copy-paste chore that often slips during busy launch weeks.

stories.title: Migrating online stores from WooCommerce to Webflow
stories.summary: Migrating a WooCommerce catalog to Webflow requires exporting data as JSON via a Next.js app to handle variations and 301 redirects. Webflow Ecommerce expects specific CSV layouts, making manual migration prone to missing variants and drifting sale prices. Orders and accounts remain as archived exports.

stories.title: Maxon adds touch support and Vision Pro preview to 3D tools
stories.summary: Maxon is adding touch support for Cinema 4D and ZBrush to the new MacBook Pro in late November. The company is also introducing a feature to preview 3D creations in Apple Vision Pro. Maxon claims this will introduce an entirely new dimension to professional creative workflows.

stories.title: Seven AI photo editors compared for 2026 workflows
stories.summary: AI photo editors have evolved beyond simple filters to include generative fill, background replacement, and batch processing. A comparison of seven tools, including Adobe Photoshop and Canva, highlights how these features cut production time. Pricing and feature limits were verified on vendor pages as of 7 November.

stories.title: Optimizing Adobe Firefly daily generation limits
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. This article outlines methods for managing and maximizing the daily generation limits provided within Adobe Firefly's free tier. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: NICMAR updates brand identity for infrastructure sector
stories.summary: NICMAR has unveiled a new brand identity to align with India’s evolving infrastructure economy. The rebranding unifies the institution’s various entities under one name, aiming to prepare professionals for emerging requirements in construction, real estate, and project management after four decades of operation.

stories.title: KRAFTON India hosts PitchFest 2026 for indie studios
stories.summary: KRAFTON India held its fourth KIGI PitchFest in Chennai, featuring eight indie studios. Participants presented playable builds and pitch decks to a jury. The event was part of the India Game Developer Conference 2026 and focused on identifying strong alignment between founders and their projects.

stories.title: Swiggy rebrands as Sweety for Diwali campaign
stories.summary: Swiggy has temporarily rebranded as Sweety to celebrate India’s love for traditional sweets. The campaign replaces the brand name across digital assets, delivery bags, and partner jerseys. Outdoor hoardings featuring the new name have been placed in prominent locations across the country.

stories.title: Swiggy discusses festive rebranding strategy
stories.summary: Swiggy’s decision to rebrand as Sweety for Diwali included changing delivery partner names in the app and updating social media profiles. The campaign, which featured a cameo from Kareena Kapoor Khan, aimed to take the cultural significance of mithai as seriously as the Indian market.

stories.title: Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath hosts national art festival
stories.summary: The Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath is hosting its national art festival, Namma Art Bengaluru, for the second time this year. The event features a wide range of creative works, continuing a series of exhibitions that celebrate innovation and the spirit of creativity across India.

stories.title: VibeCode30 highlights AI-built products in India
stories.summary: YourStory’s inaugural VibeCode30 list identifies 30 live products built with AI, ranging from healthcare to developer tools. The initiative aims to show how AI-powered coding tools are lowering technical and financial barriers, allowing non-engineers to turn ideas into working software products.

stories.title: Cao Bang Province launches armed forces logo competition
stories.summary: The Provincial Military Command of Cao Bang is organizing a logo design competition to mark the 80th anniversary of its armed forces. The contest seeks works that reflect the history and traditions of the provincial military, with submissions open to all segments of the population.

stories.title: Dien Bien province seeks a new emblem
stories.summary: Dien Bien province has launched a design contest to select an official emblem. The Organizing Committee says the winning work must reflect the locality's cultural identity and development aspirations. The province is looking for a unified brand identity to affirm its position in the process of integration.

stories.title: K G M Agro India seeks trademark for cattle feed
stories.summary: K G M Agro India has applied for brand registration of its Double Swastik Bran cattle feed. The company, which manufactures wheat flour and related products, says the move is intended to safeguard its brand identity and prevent unauthorised use of the name in the market.

stories.title: Tech Mahindra increases stake in Pininfarina
stories.summary: Tech Mahindra will raise its stake in Italian design firm Pininfarina to 92.59 percent. The Indian IT services company is acquiring 7.89 million shares for up to 9.46 million euros as the firm moves toward delisting from the Borsa Italiana. The shares are priced at 1.20 euros each.

stories.title: Delhi High Court rules on BharatPe shareholder rights
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has dismissed an appeal by Unity Bank, upholding interim protection for BharatPe's parent company, RIPL. The court has now twice declined to let the bank and its promoter proceed on reserved matters without the prior written consent of RIPL, as the agreement requires.

stories.title: Canva restructures as growth slows
stories.summary: Canva is laying off 1,271 employees, or 22 percent of its workforce, as part of a major restructuring. CEO Melanie Perkins described the decision as the most difficult in the company's 13-year history. The firm is changing team structures and skills to support its long-term ambitions.

stories.title: Rotoris raises 7.5 million dollars in Series A funding
stories.summary: Watchmaker Rotoris has raised approximately 7.5 million dollars in a Series A round led by Blume Ventures. The company, which sells its timepieces by invitation, plans to use the capital for research, production, and expanding its footprint. Its founding chapter of 2,100 numbered timepieces has sold out.

stories.title: Indian startups raise 255 million dollars
stories.summary: Indian startups raised 255 million dollars across 20 deals in the first week of November, according to Inc42 data. This represents a 96 percent increase in funding volume compared to the previous week, despite a 38 percent decline in the total number of deals completed.

stories.title: ESP Group CEO wins business award
stories.summary: Ashley Meston, CEO of ESP Group, has won the Manufacturing, Engineering and Product Design award at the Business Women Scotland Top 100 Awards. Meston joined the company 20 years ago as a customer service adviser and has led projects for clients including Network Rail and Transport for London.

stories.title: Faizan Ahmad named vice president at India TV
stories.summary: Faizan Ahmad has been promoted to vice president of business and product at India TV. A digital veteran who previously led the broadcaster’s web business, Ahmad now oversees a wider mandate across revenue and technology. The promotion follows over three years of managing the company’s web operations.

stories.title: Apoorva Kohli appointed GM of international business at TechnoSport
stories.summary: The full piece is for subscribers. Apoorva Kohli has been appointed as the general manager of international business at TechnoSport, according to reports from HR Today. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Nordisk Games appoints new CEO and CFO
stories.summary: Nordisk Games has named Stefanía Halldórsdóttir as CEO and Ásgeir Kröyer as CFO. The company is filling these roles as part of a broader industry trend of leadership transitions. The games industry continues to move people between desks at a steady pace.

stories.title: Kristen Hagen on interior design leadership
stories.summary: Kristen Hagen, a senior associate and interior design director at Mancini Duffy, continues to apply design principles learned during her time at NJIT. She currently develops firm standards and processes while working with architects to create workplaces intended to support client employees and their specific needs.

stories.title: Miami Dade College expands EPIC work-based learning model
stories.summary: Miami Dade College has scaled its Employer Provided Innovation Challenge, a model connecting students with local employers for short-term projects. Funded by the U.S. Economic Development Administration, the program pairs teams with companies for tasks in UX, web development, and applied AI. Real results are expected.

stories.title: Martine Rose named creative director at Balenciaga
stories.summary: Martine Rose has been appointed as the first woman creative director at Balenciaga. Kering chief executive Luca de Meo stated the move reflects an ambition to keep the brand at the forefront of innovation, creativity, and culture. Rose replaces Pierpaolo Piccioli after his 18-month tenure.

stories.title: Balenciaga appoints Martine Rose as creative director
stories.summary: French luxury group Kering has named British designer Martine Rose as the new creative director of Balenciaga. The appointment follows the departure of Pierpaolo Piccioli. Kering CEO Luca de Meo aims to boost sales and keep the brand at the forefront of culture amid industry-wide pressure.

stories.title: Six 2026 films use title cards as storytelling tools
stories.summary: Six films released in 2026 are using title cards as narrative devices rather than formal requirements. These intertitles, which date back to the silent era, are being used to set a mood before the action begins. The cards use specific type and material to anchor the story.

stories.title: The best movie title cards of 2026
stories.summary: The year 2026 has seen a resurgence in the use of stylised movie title cards. These openers are being used as narrative anchors to provide a beat for viewers before the action starts. The best examples function as storytelling devices rather than just aesthetic choices.

stories.title: Government considers second telecom PLI scheme
stories.summary: The government is considering a second version of its production-linked incentive scheme for the telecom industry. The proposal focuses on design-led manufacturing and domestic value addition. The Ministry of Communications is currently developing the plan before it undergoes inter-ministerial discussions for potential cabinet approval.
